# Payment Model

This file defines the Mongoose schema and model for storing payment transaction details. It outlines the structure of payment records within the application's database.

## Overview

The Payment model is responsible for persisting all information related to financial transactions, including user associations, payment provider identifiers, order details, and financial specifics like amount and currency. It is used across the application to track successful payments, typically initiated through the `payment.js` route.

## Parameters / Configuration

This model does not accept direct configuration parameters. It defines the database schema for payment records.

## Fields

The `Payment` model uses the following schema fields:

### userId

<ParamField name="userId" type="ObjectId" ref="User" required>
  The unique identifier of the user associated with this payment. This field links to the `User` model.
</ParamField>

### paymentId

<ParamField name="paymentId" type="String">
  The unique identifier provided by the payment gateway (e.g., Razorpay payment ID).
</ParamField>

### orderId

<ParamField name="orderId" type="String" required>
  The unique identifier for the order generated by the payment gateway.
</ParamField>

### status

<ParamField name="status" type="String" required>
  The current status of the payment transaction (e.g., "paid", "failed", "pending").
</ParamField>

### amount

<ParamField name="amount" type="Number" required>
  The total amount of the transaction in the smallest currency unit (e.g., paise for INR).
</ParamField>

### currency

<ParamField name="currency" type="String" required>
  The currency in which the payment was made (e.g., "INR", "USD").
</ParamField>

### receipt

<ParamField name="receipt" type="String" required>
  A unique identifier for the transaction receipt generated by the payment gateway.
</ParamField>

### notes

<ParamField name="notes" type="Object">
  An object containing additional information related to the payment.
  <Expandable title="notes properties">
    <ParamField name="notes.firstName" type="String">The first name of the user at the time of payment.</ParamField>
    <ParamField name="notes.lastName" type="String">The last name of the user at the time of payment.</ParamField>
    <ParamField name="notes.membershipType" type="String">The type of membership purchased during this transaction.</ParamField>
  </Expandable>
</ParamField>

The schema also includes `timestamps: true`, which automatically adds `createdAt` and `updatedAt` fields to each document.

## Usage Example

This model is typically used within the `payment.js` route handler to save transaction details after a successful payment confirmation.

```javascript
// Example usage in src/routes/payment.js (conceptual)
const Payment = require('../models/payment');
const mongoose = require('mongoose');

async function handleSuccessfulPayment(paymentDetails, user) {
  const newPayment = new Payment({
    userId: user._id,
    paymentId: paymentDetails.razorpay_payment_id,
    orderId: paymentDetails.razorpay_order_id,
    status: 'paid',
    amount: paymentDetails.amount,
    currency: 'INR', // Assuming INR for this example
    receipt: paymentDetails.razorpay_receipt,
    notes: {
      firstName: user.firstName,
      lastName: user.lastName,
      membershipType: 'premium', // Example membership type
    },
  });

  try {
    await newPayment.save();
    console.log('Payment record saved successfully:', newPayment._id);
    // Further actions like upgrading user subscription
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('Error saving payment record:', error);
    // Handle error appropriately
  }
}
```

## Common Errors / Troubleshooting

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="What happens if a payment record fails to save?">
    If an error occurs during the `newPayment.save()` operation, the `catch` block in the example usage will be triggered. This indicates a database issue, such as connectivity problems or schema validation errors. The error should be logged, and appropriate fallback mechanisms should be implemented, such as notifying an administrator or retrying the operation if feasible.
  </Accordion>
  <Accordion title="How are payment statuses updated?">
    The `status` field should be updated based on the responses received from the payment gateway. For instance, if the payment gateway confirms a successful transaction, the status would be set to "paid". If a transaction fails at any point, the status should be updated accordingly (e.g., "failed"). This logic typically resides within the route handler that processes the payment gateway's callbacks or webhooks.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>
